why: I checked every command in both briefs against the tracked files and the scripts in package.json. The files they name all exist: bin/greet.js, src/greet.js, test/greet.test.js, docs/index.md and .github/workflows/pages.yml. `npm test` maps to `node --test`. The node calls (`node bin/greet.js --shout ada`, `'Bob Smith'`, no name) are valid. `grep -n -- '--shout' docs/index.md` is valid because `--` ends the options. `curl -sSL … | grep -n -- '--shout'`, `gh run list --workflow pages.yml` and `gh pr view <number> --json state,mergedAt` all use real flags. The `<number>` and `<base>` placeholders stand for values that can't be known when the brief is written. They are clearly meant to be filled in, so I don't count them as broken syntax. The comparison with the base commit offers `git worktree add` or `git show <base>:path` as ways to do it, and both are valid git usage. I found no command that names a missing file, uses invalid flags or has broken syntax.
